dedupe_keys.name: manrs ixp validation tool for route server rpki filtering

description: The MANRS IXP validation tool checks whether an internet exchange point's route servers filter routes in line with Action 1 of the MANRS programme for exchanges, which asks exchanges to prevent the spread of incorrect routing information. It reads the routes held by a route server, either from an MRT RIB dump file or from the APIs of the Alice-LG or Bird's Eye looking glasses that many exchanges publish, and validates each route against RPKI data supplied as a ROA JSON file, for example from the RIPE NCC validator or rpki-client. It then prints statistics and details of any RPKI-invalid prefixes found, and in verbose mode reports every route with its validation status; a route server that follows Action 1 should hold no invalid routes. The tool was developed by DashCare for the MANRS project of the Internet Society and is written in Python 3.9 or later. Coverage: any exchange with a public looking glass or RIB dump. Format and access: Python source on GitHub, free; the licence was not shown on the repository page. Caveats: tests only RPKI origin validity, not IRR filtering or other parts of the MANRS actions; results are a snapshot at run time. Simulation uses: measuring how well route servers contain hijacks and leaks, as input to routing-security resilience scenarios. Related records: the MANRS routing security initiative case describes the programme, and ARouteServer builds filtering configurations.
